target_customer: DevOps and platform engineering teams running Kubernetes
problem: Kubernetes misconfigurations reach production; Datree runs automated policy checks in the CI pipeline via an open-source CLI.
business_model: Open-source CLI with paid SaaS policy management (freemium); pricing not verified
product_category: DevOps policy engine / Kubernetes security tooling

founders.name: Shimon Tolts
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC as CNCF Ambassador and AWS Hero. CTO title per MarketScreener; later founded Copperhelm (2024).

founders.name: Eyar Zilberman
education: Studied open-source licensing in law school (per YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Policy checks for Kubernetes manifests in CI, delivered as a Go open-source CLI plus a backend; standard engineering with the hard part being keeping policies current with Kubernetes versions.

defensibility.rationale: The CLI was open source (Apache-2.0, per aggregator listings) and policy evaluation ran locally, so copying was feasible; no network effect or data moat is evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources found list Kyverno, OPA/Gatekeeper, Conftest and Checkov as alternatives after the shutdown. Datree ceased operations in July 2023 (aggregator report); no acquisition confirmed.

market_need_then: Not independently evidenced at founding in sources I retrieved. Datree raised $3M seed (2018) and $8M Series A (Feb 2020) on the premise that Kubernetes misconfigurations were a production risk.
outcome_analysis: Datree raised about $11M across a 2018 seed and a February 2020 Series A while joining YC W20, but the YC directory lists it as inactive and an aggregator reports it stopped operating in July 2023. No company statement of the reason was found, so failure factors are left unassigned rather than guessed. Alternatives such as Kyverno and OPA remained active, and the open-source CLI was archived.
notes: Shutdown date and reason come from aggregators only (Startup Nation Central, Gappsy); no primary announcement found. One site (x-cmd) claims an acquisition in 2022, uncorroborated and not recorded. Series A lead: Blumberg and TLV per Blumberg; ZoomInfo says TLV. The seed was recorded from a search snippet of the DevOps Digest headline, page not fetched. Total ~ $11M per Startup Nation Central. Zonebourse lists a third co-founder, Arthur Schmunk, unverified.
